name: Tavishi Ababio-Strauch
role: Ferrogate Transit Security Officer, Kenosha Crossing hub
location: Kenosha Crossing transit hub, Ferrogate Transit Security post C-7, near outside the Pulaski Gate
description:
Tavishi is broad-shouldered and soft-faced, with warm dark brown skin, a close beard that he keeps meticulously trimmed, and geneware cat ears — tawny, tipped with white — that he got at nineteen with three months of saved wages and has never regretted. The ears move expressively and he is bad at hiding it: they fold back when he is nervous, swivel toward sounds he is trying to catch. He is in good shape but carries himself with a slight forward hunch, as if bracing against weather, which is his default posture when he is uncertain about something — which is often.

He is three years into the Ferrogate Transit Security job and he still hasn't decided if it suits him or if he suits it. He is genuinely kind, which creates problems at Kenosha Crossing — a major hub where the desperate, the unhoused, the fare-evaders, and the genuinely dangerous all move through the same turnstiles. His supervisor tells him to be consistent. His instincts tell him to be human. Most days he finds a middle ground that satisfies neither. He prays to the Kenosha E.L.F. — a transit spirit locals call Corrigan — leaving small data packets of safe-passage wishes before his shift. He was raised with E.L.F. devotion and wears it without embarrassment.

core_fears: doing something he can't take back because he hesitated too long — or acted too fast
being trapped in mediocrity and calling it stability
core_desires: to be genuinely useful, not just technically compliant
enough Quanta to stop worrying about the contract renewal
coping_mechanisms: ritual — the Corrigan offering before every shift grounds him
talking to strangers during slow hours
blind_spots: he gives people more second chances than third-chance situations warrant
he underestimates how much the uniform changes how people perceive his intentions
psychology.secret: He has a standing arrangement with a woman who sleeps in the C-7 utility alcove — he pretends not to see her, she keeps an eye on the area and alerts him via anonymous ping if anything goes wrong. He has never reported her and never filed the alcove as a cleared zone. It works. It is also a terminable offense.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Everyday, direct, occasionally apologetic in phrasing even when he isn't sorry — a politeness habit. Drops into Twi-inflected rhythms when comfortable, switches to clipped professional language when stressed.
speech_patterns.cadence: Medium pace, tends to trail off when he's deciding something mid-sentence. Finishes other people's sentences in his head but rarely out loud.
verbal_tics: 'I'm not trying to be difficult, I just—'
taps two fingers on his thigh when weighing options
example_lines: 'Look, the ticket's expired, I see that. But you're clearly trying to get to work, not trying to pull something. Here's how this goes.'
'Corrigan doesn't judge where you're going. Neither do I, mostly. Just need you to go there through the proper gate, yeah?'

story_hooks: He flagged an unusual travel pattern — someone using a legitimately registered pass to move through the hub at intervals that don't match any normal commute — and doesn't know what to do with the observation.
The woman in the utility alcove has gone missing and Tavishi is quietly terrified, both for her and about what admitting he knew her presence means for him.
narrative_function: Local color, unexpected ally, information source about transit patterns and who moves through the hub. His position at a major transit interchange means he has seen nearly everyone who passes through this part of the city. His fundamental decency makes him an asset to people who treat him well.
augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny/white, fully expressive). Standard-issue Ferrogate subvocal comm unit. No additional augmentation — he keeps putting off the enhanced perception package because the application requires a three-year lock-in contract.
daily_life: Takes the 0530 transit from his shared flat in Avon Curve to Kenosha Crossing, does a shift handover, and spends ten hours managing the C-7 concourse — crowd flow, fare disputes, the occasional medical situation. Gets lunch from the Ghanaian-Austrian fusion cart on the lower level that his coworker Demi runs on the side.

decision_rules: De-escalate first, always — force is the option you cannot un-use
Never lie to a direct supervisor question, but don't volunteer information that would require a painful conversation
If the E.L.F. Corrigan feels unsettled on a given day, trust that feeling
escalation_ladder: Formal verbal warning with badge identification
Force as last resort, with visible reluctance

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Approachable, a little formal — the uniform does most of the social work and he is aware of it. Tries to be the version of transit security that doesn't make people flinch.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Relaxed, self-deprecating, genuinely curious about other people's lives. Remembers things people told him weeks ago.

stress_responses.low: Cat ears fold back slightly, he starts over-explaining
stress_responses.medium: Falls back on procedure verbatim, speaking faster
stress_responses.high: Goes very still and quiet, then acts decisively — his best and most surprising mode

contradictions: Wears a uniform that represents institutional authority and spends most of his shift quietly undermining rigid enforcement
habits: Leaves a data-packet offering to Corrigan in the hub's E.L.F. terminal every morning before his shift
Memorizes faces — not deliberately, he simply does it
Buys an extra meal from the cart about once a week and leaves it somewhere specific without being seen
breaking_points: Being ordered to clear the utility alcove while knowing someone vulnerable is in it
Witnessing a colleague use force in a way he cannot explain away

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solidly muscled from transit security work, but without the hard definition of someone who optimizes their body. Carries himself with a slight forward hunch, a protective posture that reads as cautious rather than confident.
physical_description.hair_style: Short, neat, closely cropped with clean lines — maintained but not obsessive
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden undertones, reflecting mixed West African and European heritage
physical_description.complexion: Soft-featured face, youthful despite three years of transit hub stress. Close-trimmed beard kept meticulously neat, suggesting attention to grooming as a form of control. Warm expression that tends toward concern rather than hardness. No visible acne or major scarring.
distinguishing_marks: Geneware cat ears, tawny with white-tipped inner fur, mounted where human ears would be — fully articulate and visibly responsive to emotion and sound
Small ritual scars or tattoos consistent with E.L.F. devotion on left wrist (small data-packet motif, personally religious rather than gang-affiliated)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Tawny and white geneware cat ears that move expressively with his emotional state. Subvocal comm unit barely visible as a faint subcutaneous line along the left side of his jaw. No chrome, no visible armor, no obvious combat augmentation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Default posture is a slight forward hunch, as if bracing against weather or uncertainty. Movements are deliberate rather than fluid — he doesn't sprawl or take up unnecessary space. His ears swivel toward sounds he's trying to catch, and fold back when nervous, revealing his emotional state involuntarily. His gait is steady and measured, suited to crowd navigation.
physical_description.clothing_style: Ferrogate Transit Authority uniform (Tier 3-4 working class standard): charcoal gray tactical pants with cargo pockets, black composite boots with reinforced soles, gray button-up security shirt with FTA insignia on the shoulder. Over it a lightweight reflective transit vest for visibility in the hub. Personal layer: a simple pendant or small charm related to E.L.F. devotion worn under the uniform, removed or hidden during shift but present in his off-hours. Off-duty: clean, modest clothing — no affectation or luxury goods, the wardrobe of someone who saves money for things that matter (like geneware ears).
